title: Too much stuff
paragraphs: Do you have too many pairs of shoes or old gadgets lying around the house? I'm sure many of us have a lot of things that we don't really use and when things get out of hand, it's really time for a spring clean to declutter our lives.

However, deciding which items to get rid of can be tricky especially if you are materialistic, believing that physical possessions are the most important thing in life. Also, some people are sentimental about letting go of their personal property. But if you haven't got room in your house to move, it's time to evaluate what is really important to you and decide what are your prized possessions and what is just junk.

Instead of just chucking it away and filling up landfill sites, items could be recycled or given to a charity to re-sell. You could also make some money by using websites where people are willing to pay for second-hand goods. Some people have taken a minimalist approach, deliberately trying to keep life simple. Bea Johnson, author of Zero Waste Home, has done this. She says "we've asked really true questions, and evaluated every single thing that we have. There is nothing that we overlooked. I even came to look at my vegetable peeler for example and asked myself, 'do I really need that vegetable peeler?'"

Of course, if you're a shopaholic or a fashion-victim it's hard to stop buying and shopping online makes purchasing stuff very easy. James Wallman is a writer and journalist - he questions what we actually need. He says "I'm not anti-stuff - stuff is good. I'm anti too much stuff and I'm anti the wrong stuff. Don't go out and buy that labelled good that you think is going to make people think something more of you. That's not going to make you happy."

This sounds like good advice. It's good to take stock of what we have and what we really need. But there are still some things I just can't face parting company with; my CD collection, even though I now download my music, and my childhood teddy bear. What about you - have you got something that you just can't throw away?

vocabulary.entry: gadget [n.] /ˈɡædʒɪt/ 小器具；小装置
vocabulary.example: He loves buying the latest electronic gadgets.
vocabulary.translation: 他喜欢购买最新的电子小玩意儿。

vocabulary.entry: out of hand [phr.] /aʊt əv hænd/ 失控 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The party got out of hand and the police were called.
vocabulary.translation: 派对失控了，警察被叫来了。

vocabulary.entry: declutter [v.] /diːˈklʌtə/ 整理；清理 (口语)
vocabulary.example: I need to declutter my wardrobe and get rid of old clothes.
vocabulary.translation: 我需要整理衣柜，扔掉旧衣服。

vocabulary.entry: get rid of [phr.] /ɡet rɪd əv/ 摆脱；处理掉 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: It's time to get rid of these old newspapers.
vocabulary.translation: 是时候处理掉这些旧报纸了。

vocabulary.entry: materialistic [adj.] /məˌtɪəriəˈlɪstɪk/ 物质主义的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Modern society is often criticized for being too materialistic.
vocabulary.translation: 现代社会常被批评过于物质主义。

vocabulary.entry: sentimental [adj.] /ˌsentɪˈmentl/ 多愁善感的；怀旧的
vocabulary.example: She is sentimental about her childhood home.
vocabulary.translation: 她对童年的家充满眷恋。

vocabulary.entry: prized [adj.] /praɪzd/ 珍贵的；宝贵的
vocabulary.example: Her prized possession is a necklace from her grandmother.
vocabulary.translation: 她珍贵的财产是祖母送的一条项链。

vocabulary.entry: junk [n.] /dʒʌŋk/ 垃圾；废旧物品
vocabulary.example: The attic is full of junk that we never use.
vocabulary.translation: 阁楼里堆满了我们从不使用的废旧物品。

vocabulary.entry: chuck away [phr.] /tʃʌk əˈweɪ/ 扔掉；丢弃 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Don't chuck away that old chair – it could be restored.
vocabulary.translation: 别扔掉那把旧椅子——它还可以修复。

vocabulary.entry: landfill site [n.] /ˈlændfɪl saɪt/ 垃圾填埋场 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: The waste is transported to a landfill site outside the city.
vocabulary.translation: 这些废物被运往城外的垃圾填埋场。

vocabulary.entry: second-hand goods [n. pl.] /ˈsekənd hænd ɡʊdz/ 二手商品 (单数: second-hand good)
vocabulary.example: You can find great bargains at second-hand goods stores.
vocabulary.translation: 你可以在二手商品店找到很划算的东西。

vocabulary.entry: re-sell [v.] /ˌriːˈsel/ 转售
vocabulary.example: He buys old furniture and re-sells it for a profit.
vocabulary.translation: 他购买旧家具然后转售获利。

vocabulary.entry: minimalist [adj.] /ˈmɪnɪməlɪst/ 极简主义的
vocabulary.example: She adopted a minimalist lifestyle, owning only the essentials.
vocabulary.translation: 她采用了极简主义的生活方式，只拥有必需品。

vocabulary.entry: keep life simple [phr.] /kiːp laɪf ˈsɪmpl/ 让生活保持简单 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Moving to the countryside helped him keep life simple.
vocabulary.translation: 搬到乡下帮助他让生活保持简单。

vocabulary.entry: overlook [v.] /ˌəʊvəˈlʊk/ 忽略；忽视
vocabulary.example: He overlooked a key detail in the contract.
vocabulary.translation: 他忽略了合同中的一个关键细节。

vocabulary.entry: vegetable peeler [n.] /ˈvedʒtəbəl ˈpiːlə/ 削皮器
vocabulary.example: A good vegetable peeler makes food preparation easier.
vocabulary.translation: 一把好的削皮器让备餐更轻松。

vocabulary.entry: shopaholic [n.] /ˌʃɒpəˈhɒlɪk/ 购物狂 (口语)
vocabulary.example: Her credit card debt shows she is a shopaholic.
vocabulary.translation: 她的信用卡债务表明她是个购物狂。

vocabulary.entry: fashion-victim [n.] /ˈfæʃən ˈvɪktɪm/ 时尚受害者 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: A fashion-victim buys every trend without thinking.
vocabulary.translation: 时尚受害者会不加思考地购买每一种潮流单品。

vocabulary.entry: labelled good [n.] /ˈleɪbəld ɡʊd/ 名牌商品 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: He only buys labelled goods to impress his friends.
vocabulary.translation: 他只买名牌商品来给朋友留下印象。

vocabulary.entry: take stock of [phr.] /teɪk stɒk əv/ 评估；审视 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: We need to take stock of our financial situation.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要评估我们的财务状况。

vocabulary.entry: parting company with [phr.] /ˈpɑːtɪŋ ˈkʌmpəni wɪð/ 与……分离；舍弃 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: It was difficult parting company with his old car.
vocabulary.translation: 舍弃他的旧车很难。

vocabulary.entry: download [v.] /ˌdaʊnˈləʊd/ 下载
vocabulary.example: You can download the app for free from the website.
vocabulary.translation: 你可以从网站免费下载这个应用程序。

vocabulary.entry: let go of [phr.] /let ɡəʊ əv/ 放开；舍弃 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: It's time to let go of the past and move forward.
vocabulary.translation: 是时候放下过去，向前看了。

sentences.chinese: 你家里是不是有太多双鞋子或者旧的小器具到处乱放呢？

sentences.english: Also, some people are sentimental about letting go of their personal property.

sentences.english: But if you haven't got room in your house to move, it's time to evaluate what is really important to you and decide what are your prized possessions and what is just junk.
sentences.chinese: 但是如果你家里连走动的空间都没有了，那就该评估一下什么对你来说才是真正重要的，并且确定哪些是你珍贵的财产，哪些只是垃圾。

sentences.english: Instead of just chucking it away and filling up landfill sites, items could be recycled or given to a charity to re-sell.
sentences.chinese: 与其只是把东西扔掉，填满垃圾填埋场，不如把这些物品回收利用，或者捐给慈善机构再出售。

sentences.english: You could also make some money by using websites where people are willing to pay for second-hand goods.
sentences.chinese: 你也可以通过一些网站赚钱，在这些网站上，人们愿意购买二手物品。

sentences.english: Some people have taken a minimalist approach, deliberately trying to keep life simple.
sentences.chinese: 有些人采取了极简主义的方式，刻意让生活保持简单。

sentences.english: Bea Johnson, author of Zero Waste Home, has done this.

sentences.english: She says "we've asked really true questions, and evaluated every single thing that we have.
sentences.chinese: 她说：“我们问了非常真实的问题，并评估我们所拥有的每一件东西。

sentences.chinese: 我们没有忽略任何东西。

sentences.chinese: 比如，我甚至会看着我的削皮器，问自己，‘我真的需要那个削皮器吗？’”

sentences.chinese: 詹姆斯·沃尔曼是一位作家兼记者，他质疑我们真正需要的东西是什么。

sentences.english: He says "I'm not anti-stuff - stuff is good.
sentences.chinese: 他说：“我并不反对物质——物质是好的。

sentences.english: I'm anti too much stuff and I'm anti the wrong stuff.
sentences.chinese: 我反对的是太多的物质，以及错误的物质。

sentences.english: Don't go out and buy that labelled good that you think is going to make people think something more of you.
sentences.chinese: 不要出去买那些你认为会让别人对你另眼相看的名牌商品。

sentences.english: That's not going to make you happy."
sentences.chinese: 那不会让你快乐。”

sentences.english: This sounds like good advice.
sentences.chinese: 这听起来是很好的建议。

sentences.english: It's good to take stock of what we have and what we really need.
sentences.chinese: 评估一下我们所拥有的和我们真正需要的东西是有好处的。

sentences.english: But there are still some things I just can't face parting company with; my CD collection, even though I now download my music, and my childhood teddy bear.
sentences.chinese: 但是仍然有一些东西我实在无法割舍，比如我的CD收藏，尽管我现在都是下载音乐，还有我童年时的泰迪熊。
